newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares climb after new government voted.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares climb after new government voted.

text.p: Slovenian shares bounced higher on Friday as the market welcomed the approval of a new government and on hopes that the end to the political impasse may encourage foreign investors to return.
The new government was voted in late on Thursday.
"I think the time of extensive foreign buying is approaching," said Gregor Pajic, a trader at brokerage Certius.
* The SBI index rose 35.38 points to 1,431.06.
* Overall 15 shares rose, one fell and 10 were untraded.
* Drug maker Lek's A issue was the most actively traded share, firming 1.57 percent to an average price of 28,401 tolars on volume of 7,736 shares.
